0004. Every outside submission is a GitHub issue form in the repo that owns it

Personal project. Research and learning only. Not for production. No warranty.
  • Built on my own time for research and learning. Not affiliated with, endorsed by or supported by my employer or Microsoft.
  • Don't run any of it in production or against tenants that matter. Test in a dedicated lab subscription and tenant first.
  • Provided "as is", without warranty of any kind, under each repo's license. You use it at your own risk and own the Azure charges it incurs.
  • Contributions and forks are welcome and encouraged. See Contribute.

Context and Problem Statement

Three surfaces will ask outsiders to send things in: the credits and contributors page, the standards and research review UI, and the support mailbot. What they send (evidence, research, research requests, feedback and disputes, bug reports, feature requests) has to reach the right repo in a reviewable shape, without a server, a secret or personal data held by us. How should submissions get in?

Considered Options

  • GitHub issue forms in each owning repo, vendored from one canonical set in avd-ops, with one routing table and a link builder the three surfaces share
  • A form endpoint (Staticman or a small Worker) that opens issues or pull requests with a bot token
  • A hosted form or helpdesk service

Decision Outcome

Chosen option: "GitHub issue forms", because GitHub Issues is already the tracker, the forms need no server and no token, GitHub sign-in is the spam barrier, and the family already uses issue forms for its KB and for avd-assess evidence. The design is docs/submissions-spec.md.

Consequences

  • Good, because it costs nothing, holds no personal data beyond the person's own issue, and a person reads every submission before anything acts on it (accepted is applied by hand).
  • Good, because one routing table names repos from repos.json, so moves and renames change one file.
  • Bad, because a submitter needs a GitHub account; the mailbot is the path for anyone without one, and Nick opens the issue.
  • Bad, because forms are vendored into each repo and can drift; family.yml checks them weekly.

More Information

A repo with its own .github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/ ignores an org .github repo's defaults, and every family repo but avd-current-state has one, so defaults alone can't share the forms. Never put the submitter's text in a prefilled issue URL: it would sit in browser history and referrers (mailbot red team finding 6). Revisit if outside submissions outgrow manual triage.
